correctness.rationale: The primary staircase theorem identifies A(t) uniquely for irrational t and gives ordered rational plateaux including endpoints. The series jump can also be checked directly: on approach from below to reduced p/q, floor(kt) drops by one only for q dividing k, moving the contribution at k=lq−1 to k=lq with common weight μ^(lp−1); summing the resulting geometric difference gives the frozen jump. For fixed [u,v] strictly inside (0,r), θ=λ max(1,μ^v)<1 even with an expanding right branch. This majorizes each summand by θ^k. For μ<1, telescoping μ^floor(kt) gives denominator ≥1−λ and truncation only increases it; for μ≥1 the denominator is at least one. This bound and a finite upper bound give the required Lipschitz upper estimate and positive exponential lower estimate on plateau widths. The truncation through k=N is constant between rational thresholds of denominator ≤N+1; O(N²) cells, each with image variation at most one Lipschitz tail, give the upper cover. Möbius inversion over the wedge u<p/q<v gives 3(v−u)Q²/π²+O(Q log Q). For Q=floor(log(1/ε)/(2|log s_*|)), each of these plateaux eventually exceeds ε in length; an irrational image between consecutive plateaux gives M(Q)−1 pairwise ε-separated points. This proves the matching lower bound, including the specified length convention. The example's S values at 1/2 and its left limit are 2 and 1, yielding [2/3,7/10]. Zero Hausdorff dimension on the full open parameter range follows by countable exhaustion in rotation number, not a global box bound at the endpoint. The recorded finite algebra checks are supporting, not the source of the two asymptotic bounds.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A dimension-zero statement, or even an upper Hausdorff gauge bound, does not furnish matching equal-length covers and packing. The single-slope results do not dominate the expanding right-branch scope.

evidence: For μ=1 the plateau width (1−λ)²λ^(q−1)/(1−λ^q) yields log² many large gaps by Farey counting; the existing O(N²) cover with O(Nλ^N) tail gives the upper half. The μ=1 covering order is thus a short consequence, even though it is not printed as such.

For the general case the new estimate requires uniform control of the Möbius denominators, a compact-window exponential tail using average rather than branchwise contraction, and a Farey packing at a common physical scale.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Credit the actual implication in the single-slope case. The general prior staircase gives exact pointwise information, but turning it into the two-sided covering law through an expanding branch needs both the new uniform tail argument and gap separation count.

originality.rationale: The single-slope subcase and basic zero-dimension consequences have prior coverage; the supported distinct claim is the matching uniform-scale bound throughout the admissible two-slope family on compact interior windows, including the expanding branch. The primary inverse-staircase formulas are prior; separate counting and uniform estimates turn those formulas into the sharp quantitative law. No covering theorem matching that full scope was identified in the inspected passages.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently formulated two-slope quantitative results may exist. The basic staircase, the single-slope covering order and prior zero-dimension results are not claimed as distinct contributions.
